recipe.name: Chal'er Atta'r Rooti
directions: In a kadai, bring water to a boil. Mix in salt.
When the water is bubbling, turn the flame to low, and add in the rice flour while constantly stirring it in.
Continue mixing and cooking on low heat until all the water has absorbed.
Once you notice that there are no raw rice-flour patches visible and that the rice flour has completely cooked off, transfer the choux to a work surface.
Knead it while it is still hot, dipping your hands frequently in some room-temperature water.
Cover and set the dough to rest.
After an hour, give it a second knead using dampened hands. Once again cover and set it to rest.
When the dough is completely cool (after about another hour), give it a third and final knead before dividing it into 13 equal portions of about 70 g each.
Dust your hand with flour and flatten each ball of dough, pinching the sides to seal them in.
Roll on a bed of rice flour to about 24-cm diameter.
Cook on a hot iron skillet ensuring that there are no blisters on the rooti.
Reserve the cooked rootis between banana leaves to keep them fresh longer.
Serve with murgir lal jhol or chhola'r dal'er halwa.

ingredients.name: Rice Flour (made From Non-parboiled, Aatop Rice) + Extra for Dusting
